title: Investigation of new diagnostic methods for the detection of mycobacteria
summary:
The goal of this project is to evaluate two diagnostic approaches in patients with tuberculosis, NTM disease, or individuals at high risk for these infections, such as patients receiving strong immunosuppressive therapy after organ transplantation.

On the one hand, a novel diagnostic method based on ELISpot technology will be evaluated to assess the immune response to NTM by analyzing cytokine profiles. ELISpot assays are Interferon Gamma Release Assays (IGRAs), similar to the QuantiFERON Gold In-Tube test, and are already in clinical use for tuberculosis diagnostics. However, their application for diagnosing NTM infections has so far been scarcely investigated (DOI: 10.3389/fmicb.2021.692395).
To this end, patients with confirmed NTM infection, confirmed tuberculosis, and individuals at high risk for NTM infection (i.e., immunosuppressed patients) will be recruited. During an outpatient visit or inpatient stay, an additional blood sample will be collected during routine blood draws. The samples will then be analyzed using the novel NTM ELISpot test in appropriately equipped laboratories.
Subproject 1 will be conducted across four sites.

On the other hand, a non-invasive breath test for the diagnosis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis will be evaluated. This project is a collaboration with the Kertzscher research group at the Institute for Cardiovascular Computer-Assisted Medicine, Charité (funded through BIH Spark Track 1).
The goal of this research is to develop a new point-of-care test based on gold nanoparticles (GNPs) coated with antibodies that aggregate upon binding to bacteria, resulting in a color change in a detection solution.
To support test development, it is first necessary to determine whether and how many bacteria can be isolated using the current sampling method. The primary goal is to assess whether a sufficient number of bacteria can be filtered from exhaled air. Subsequently, the diagnostic accuracy of the test will be compared with the current standard of care. We plan to enroll patients with confirmed tuberculosis up to a maximum of 10 days after the start of therapy, as well as patients with confirmed NTM disease (serving as a negative control group).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Tuberculosis infection, NTM infection, or a high-risk profile for either of the two aforementioned conditions
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to consent, pregnancy, and other medical reasons contraindicating blood collection
